items.title: Committee to inspect Valagerahalli Lake
points: The Lokayukta has acted on a petition filed by local residents, who raised concerns over the deteriorating condition of Valagerahalli Lake and the health hazards it poses.

After examining the complaints and a report submitted by the executive engineer of the lake division of the Bengaluru West City Corporation, the Lokayukta observed that sewage was entering the lake along with rainwater.
The Lokayukta expressed concern over the lack of adequate action by the authorities to prevent pollution and protect the lake.

A joint inspection committee comprising the Chief Engineer (TAC) of the Karnataka Lokayukta, Superintendent of Police-1, Karnataka Lokayukta, and officials of the Karnataka State Pollution Control Board has been constituted.
The committee has been directed to inspect the lake, assess its present condition, and submit a report with recommendations by November 30.
The Lokayukta said action would be initiated against officials found guilty of dereliction of duty if steps were not taken to resolve the issue.

items.title: IISc researchers combine antibiotics to tackle drug-resistant TB
points: According to the IISc, TB caused by M. tuberculosis, continues to remain one of the world’s most persistent health challenges.
Now, researchers at the Department of Biochemistry have now identified a strategy to restore the effectiveness of isoniazid – by combining it with another antibiotic, vancomycin.

To tackle this problem, we started exploring ways to rescue the drug by reversing resistance,” said Nagasuma Chandra, Professor at the Department of Biochemistry and corresponding author of the study published in Microbiology Spectrum.

The researchers tested the combination of isoniazid and vancomycin against clinical isolates of M. tuberculosis obtained from patient sputum samples with drug-resistant TB, in collaboration with the National Tuberculosis Institute, Bengaluru.
Most of the isolates showed more than 90% reduction in bacterial growth under the combination treatment.

The researchers then tested the drug combination in a mouse model infected with an MDR M. tuberculosis in collaboration with Amit Singh, Professor at the Centre for Infectious Disease Research (CIDR) and Department of Microbiology and Cell Biology (MCB), IISc.

Cool Eternity is the latest addition to the Cool Carriers fleet.

Her five refrigerated holds provide approximately 905,000 cubic feet of cargo capacity across nine cooling zones.

items.title: Eurozone industrial production ticked up but still unimpressive in September

Weakness among energy-intensive sectors continues, although September saw a small production increase.
The most notable moves in September were a sharp decline in computer and electronics production, which had been a strong performer in 2026, and an uptick in motor vehicle production.
Pharma also underperformed again after a very strong second quarter.
This mixed bag was also visible by country, with strong performances in Germany, Spain and Italy, but declines in the Netherlands, France and most notably Ireland.

items.title: China Fixed Investment Contraction Deepens
points: China’s fixed-asset investment dropped by 8.1% year-on-year in the January-October 2026 period, deepening from a 7.2% fall recorded in the first nine months of the year and worse than market expectations of a 7% decline.

Weak property investment remained the primary drag, slumping 21.6%, compared with 20.6% in January-September, amid tepid housing demand, falling property prices, and tighter financing conditions for developers.
Investment in infrastructure (-5.1% vs -4.2%) and manufacturing (-2.9% vs -2.1%) continued to decline.
Investment across all three sub-industries also dropped further: primary industry (-6.1% vs -3.9%), secondary industry (-3.6% vs -2.7%), and tertiary industry (-10.9% vs -10%).
Excluding the property sector, fixed-asset investment declined by 5.1% in the first ten months of the year, following a 4.2% drop in January-September.
On a monthly basis, fixed-asset investment fell by 2.93% in October, reversing a 0.85% increase in September.

items.title: Greek shipowners put Brussels on the spot over IMO deadlock
points: Greek shipowners have launched a fresh attack on Brussels ahead of the next round of international shipping emissions negotiations, accusing the European Union of putting its own regulatory interests ahead of a global agreement.

Union of Greek Shipowners president Melina Travlos warned on Monday that the EU’s unwillingness to compromise risks pushing the International Maritime Organization into another deadlock when talks resume in London next week.

Travlos said there had been no meaningful progress since the previous negotiating round in September and questioned whether Brussels was more interested in preserving its regional carbon regulations and the revenue they generate than securing a worldwide deal.

Greece and three other EU member states, together controlling around 70% of Europe’s shipping fleet according to Travlos, have repeatedly called for greater flexibility in the European negotiating position.
The intervention comes ahead of a November 23–27 IMO working group meeting, followed by the Marine Environment Protection Committee’s 85th session from November 30 to December 3.

items.title: Decline in number of Indian students studying in U.S.
points: According to The Open Doors 2026 Report on International Educational Exchange, most Indian students were studying at the graduate level, with up to 116,609 studying at various universities in 2025-26.
This was a 34% decline in comparison to the prior year.
There were also 39,711 Indian students studying at the undergraduate level, one percent lower than the previous year.
The report states that international graduate students were the largest among the different student groups studying at various levels in the U.S. , numbering 423,078.
Among graduate students, a decline of 13% was primarily driven by a decline in students pursuing master’s degrees, up to 22%, the report states.
In contrast, doctoral student totals increased by 3% and undergraduate enrolments remained stable at 356,165 students, with a modest 0.3% decline.
“The number of new international students, those at their college or university for the first time, decreased by 18% to 228,123,” the report states.

items.title: Navy chief says over 85% of Pakistan's military hardware is Chinese: ‘Fully aware of their capabilities’
points: Over 85 per cent of Pakistan's military equipment comes from China, Chief of the Naval Staff Admiral Krishna Swaminathan said on Monday.

At the ANI National Security Summit 3.0 in New Delhi, Swaminathan said India was closely monitoring the capabilities of neighbouring countries but maintained that Pakistan and China were viewed separately at the national level.
"The fact that more than 85 per cent of the hardware Pakistan currently has in its armed forces is of Chinese origin, with some of Turkish origin but largely Chinese, is something we take note of.

Addressing concerns over a possible China-Pakistan two-front challenge, the navy chief said the Indian Navy did not view maritime security through the conventional framework of one-front or two-front wars.
The Navy chief said India was aware of the growing importance of submarine warfare, particularly in the Indian Ocean Region, and was strengthening its own underwater fleet.
Swaminathan also stressed that India did not club China and Pakistan together while assessing its security and diplomatic relationships.

items.title: Rahul Gandhi, INDIA bloc seek Supreme Court nod to question Election Commission on 48 SIR-related questions
points: The Opposition has approached the Supreme Court, seeking permission to question the Election Commission of India (ECI) over the controversy surrounding the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and its decision-making process.

A list of 48 questions submitted by the petitioners seeks details about who ordered the nationwide revision, how key decisions were taken and whether there were disagreements among the Election Commissioners, according to a post shared by the Congress on X.
The Congress alleged that the Election Commission had failed to address questions repeatedly raised over 'vote theft' in its affidavit filed before the Supreme Court.

points: Arion Kurtaj, the hacker behind the major 2022 GTA 6 leak, has pleaded guilty to hacking Rockstar Games and several other companies.
The 21-year-old appeared at Woolwich Crown Court on Monday, November 16, after being deemed fit to stand trial following his release from a secure hospital.
On November 16, Kurtaj pleaded guilty to the Rockstar breach that leaked GTA 6.
Kurtaj was a member of the Lapsus$ hacking group when he breached Rockstar’s systems in September 2022.
He stole around 90 clips showing nearly an hour of unfinished GTA 6 gameplay and threatened to release the game’s source code unless Rockstar contacted him.
Rockstar told the court that recovering from the breach cost around $5 million, along with thousands of hours of staff time.
A later assessment found Kurtaj fit to stand trial for the GTA 6 hacker allegations by Rockstar Games.

items.title: Jones Act Waiver Extended Another 90 Days as U.S. Maritime Groups Sound Alarm
points: The Trump administration has extended its emergency Jones Act waiver for another 90 days, allowing foreign-flagged vessels to continue transporting oil and other commodities between U.S. ports under a case-by-case approval process, despite growing…

The extension, confirmed Friday by U.S. Customs and Border Protection, takes effect November 16 and runs through February 14, 2027, prolonging what has become the longest-running waiver in the history of the century-old shipping law.
CBP said the Department of Homeland Security approved the third extension of the waiver originally issued March 17 at the request of the Department of War.
The Jones Act generally requires cargo transported between U.S. ports to move aboard American-built, American-owned and American-crewed vessels.
The American Maritime Partnership (AMP) called for the waiver to end while urging strict enforcement of the existing approval process.

The Offshore Marine Service Association (OMSA), which represents 170 companies and approximately 12,000 American workers, issued a sharper warning, arguing that repeated exemptions are eroding confidence in the domestic maritime industry.

items.title: SEBI sets up sub-group to review IPO, fundraising regulations
points: The review is aimed at simplifying and rationalising regulatory requirements for companies raising capital, reducing duplicative disclosures and procedures, and improving regulatory clarity and consistency.
The panel will examine eligibility conditions for companies seeking to raise capital through different routes, including IPOs, FPOs, preferential issues and QIPs.
It will also review lock-in requirements applicable to promoters, pre-issue capital and securities allotted through preferential issues.
The sub-group will review Chapters II, IIA, IV, V and VI of the ICDR Regulations, along with the relevant schedules and related regulatory directions.
The sub-group will be chaired by Ashish Chauhan, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

Its members include Gopalan S Raghavan, Executive Director at BSE; Prasanna Kumar D, President of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India; and Pawan Kumar Chandak, President of the Institute of Company Secretaries of India.
Other areas of review include application, allocation and allotment mechanisms, disclosure requirements in offer documents, pricing norms and the price discovery framework.

The A5 sits on a new platform, is larger than its predecessor and brings a completely different cabin.

The A5 will be the second model in Audi’s three-car product push, after the new-generation Q3 launched in October.
For Audi, the A5 matters because its entry-luxury sedan line-up has needed a genuinely new product for some time.
A wider grille, slimmer headlamps, pronounced wheel arches and a gently sloping roof give the new car a sportier appearance than the rather conservative A4.

items.title: Delhi government allows voter ID, driving licence for citizen services, makes Aadhaar authentication voluntary
points: The Delhi government will not deny any service to residents due to lack of Aadhaar authentication, allowing verification through alternative documents such as voter ID, driving licence and passport, an official notification said.
The notification issued recently by the information technology department under the Aadhaar Act, 2016, makes Aadhaar authentication "voluntary" for residents, it said.

The IT department is now mandated to inform Aadhaar number holders about alternative and viable means of identification and ensure that no service is denied if they are unable to undergo Aadhaar authentication or refuse to do so, the notification said.
Aadhaar authentication will remain voluntary for the Unified Citizen Data Platform (UCDP), it said.

The alternative identity documents specified in the notification include voter identity card, driving licence, passport and any other photo identity card issued by the Central or state governments, it said.
The department will also be required to obtain the consent of the Aadhaar holders before carrying out the authentication.

items.title: JFE Engineering wins offshore wind maintenance contract
points: Japanese engineering company JFE Engineering and local partner Akita Maritime Service have secured a five-year maintenance contract for Japan’s 315MW Oga-Katagami-Akita offshore wind farm.

The joint venture will provide inspection and maintenance services for the project’s balance-of-plant infrastructure, covering 21 monopile foundations, subsea cables, onshore substations, and transmission lines.
The contract excludes maintenance of the wind turbines themselves and includes options for renewal and extension over the project’s operating life.
JFE said it was the first long-term balance-of-plant maintenance contract awarded for a fixed-bottom offshore wind farm selected through Japan’s national offshore wind auction system.

The work was carried out in cooperation with Norwegian engineering contractor Aibel, which secured the front-end engineering and design (FEED) contract for the FPSO topsides from Equinor and its partners in October.
KBR’s scope covered naval architecture, structural engineering, marine systems, and vessel layout design, with particular emphasis on the harsh environmental conditions expected in the Barents Sea.
The design underwent extensive model basin and wind tunnel testing, including trials using a 1:60-scale model of the proposed FPSO.
According to KBR, the tests demonstrated that the vessel could protect its accommodation areas from green water in extreme conditions, including waves approaching 21 m.
Wisting is located approximately 310 km north of Hammerfest in water depths of around 400 m and contains estimated recoverable resources of just under 500m barrels of oil equivalent.

items.title: SwissChemGas joins VLAC ordering rush with Hengli pair

The move would mark SwissChemGas’ entry into the VLAC newbuilding market, expanding its involvement in gas shipping beyond its established LPG trading business.
SwissChemGas traces its roots to 1997, when it was established as SwissGas within Greek shipping group SwissMarine, initially focusing on LNG and LPG trading in the Mediterranean.
The company expanded into larger LPG cargoes following its acquisition of ContiChem, the gas trading arm of Continental Grain, in 2002.
It subsequently scaled back operations before returning to the fully refrigerated LPG market in 2016.

items.title: Sebi weighs biometrics, geotagging for trading terminals
points: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) and the Industry Standards Forum (ISF) are discussing biometric authentication and geotagging of trading terminals to curb unauthorized access and dabba trading, according to two people aware of the matter.
“Sebi thinks that only the dealer should be able to operate the terminal and the location of such use should be fixed and tracked,” said one of the officials.
“The objective is to avoid dabba trading and increase the accountability of the ones authorized to use trading terminals.

Under the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Stock Brokers) Regulations, 1992, brokers may incur monetary penalties for allowing the use of trading terminals to unauthorized persons or at unauthorized locations.

A May 2023 NSE circular said that computer-to-computer link (CTCL) terminals could be used only by approved persons, including employees of brokers, partners, directors, registered authorized persons and their employees.
